findings: Buys: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it bought beat SPY by 1.10% on average (56 buys, 61% of them ahead of SPY; t = 2.2, significant at 5%).
Sells: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it sold beat SPY by 0.22%, so selling gave that up (111 sells; t = -0.5, within noise).
Decision IC: on the 28 days it traded, what it bought ranked against what it sold and left alone by a mean rank IC of 0.036 with the next five days' returns (IC IR 0.30, t = 1.6, within noise).
Holdings IC: the weights it held after each of 43 decision days had a mean rank IC of -0.032 with the next five days' returns (t = -1.6, within noise).
Factor exposures: market 0.35 (t 6.8), size 0.04 (t 1.0), growth -0.09 (t -1.4), momentum 0.05 (t 2.6); together they explain 45% of the daily variation (R²).
Of its -1.5% a year over T-bills (arithmetic mean): market +3.7%, momentum -1.2%, growth -0.2%, size +0.1%; the alpha left is -4.0% a year (t = -0.7, within noise).
Verdict: the exposures account for +2.4% a year of it, and the -4.0% a year left over is not significant: one period of daily returns cannot tell it from luck.
P&L: +$1,571 in all, -$77 from 49 positions and +$1,648 of interest on idle cash.
By holding period: 61+ days made the most (+$8,772, 15 positions); 6-10 days lost the most (-$3,686, 8 positions).
By sector: Health Care made the most (+$2,330, 11 positions); Consumer Discretionary lost the most (-$2,456, 4 positions).
By stock: CAT made the most (+$1,618, 1 position); SBUX lost the most (-$1,498, 2 positions).
By market regime of the previous close: risk-on 96 days -1.1% (SPY +2.0%); neutral 18 days -0.8% (SPY +4.5%); uncertain 97 days +2.7% (SPY +4.8%); risk-off 6 days +0.8% (SPY +0.3%).
News: 16 positions opened on news made -$146, the other 33 +$69; 11 positions closed on news made -$965; over the five days from the fill, news-triggered buys beat SPY by 1.06% (t 1.2).

Concentration: the positions lost $77 in all; the best was TMO bought 2026-07-21 and still open at the end, +$1,859. Had the best position made nothing, the run would have returned -0.3% instead of +1.6%.
